sections.html:
Part of the Charleston metro area, Dorchester County runs from St. George, the seat, in the northwest down to the busy Summerville and Ladson corridor in the southeast, where most people live. It spans 571.18 square miles (568.59 of them land) and borders Bamberg, Orangeburg, Berkeley, Charleston and Colleton counties. The 2020 count was 161,540 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 178,397.

Summerville, Ladson and Lincolnville each cross into a neighboring county, so a mailing address near a town line may point to the wrong county. Find the parcel's tax map number first, then look for the bill.

Age matters in this housing stock. A home near the Summerville Historic District will need different repairs from a subdivision house built in the last twenty years, and the inspection report usually drives the buyer's requests.

The deadline for real property tax is January 15, with penalties starting the next day. Payment season opens September 30, and bills have gone out in mid October in earlier years. Section 12-45-180 lets the penalties stack.

If unpaid byAdded penaltyRunning total
After January 153%3%

After March 16, an unpaid bill is handed to the Delinquent Tax Office with the 15 percent penalty already attached. One narrow exception exists. When ownership changed mid-year and the notice reached only the previous owner, the treasurer shall waive penalties for a new owner who got no timely notice. Treat that as a long shot, and after any purchase or sale, verify who the bill is addressed to.

Payment works online through the county taxes portal, at the St. George or Summerville Treasurer's offices, or by mail in the return envelope. A bill that has not shown up by November 10 is a reason to phone the Assessor's Office at (843) 832-0162 and check the mailing address.

Each office has a distinct task: the Assessor sets the value, the Auditor figures the bill, and the Treasurer takes the payment.

  • Assessor and legal residence: (843) 832-0162, with offices in St. George and Summerville. The St. George address is 201 Johnston Street, St. George, SC 29477.
  • Treasurer: handles current property tax. Send questions to Treasurer@DorchesterCountySC.gov.
  • Delinquent Tax Office: 201 Johnston Street, St. George, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Phone (843) 563-0110 or (843) 832-0110, or email delinquenttax@dorchestercountysc.gov.

The county's Treasurer's Office page and delinquent tax page carry current details. Procedures shift over time, so confirm a phone number with each office before you act.

sections.h2: What a sale does to the assessment
sections.html:
A sale usually brings a new appraisal. The Property Tax Reform Act of 2006 made most transfers assessable, which means the county values the property at market as of December 31 of the year it sold. Expect the next owner's bill to look different from yours.

Owner-occupied homes, manufactured homes among them, qualify for the 4 percent legal residence rate, one per owner. Report a change of owner, mailing address or use to the Assessor inside six months. Buyers need to wait for the deed to be recorded with the Register of Deeds before applying, or the application may be returned.

Mobile homes follow separate rules. Registration is due within 15 days of buying one in the county or moving one here. A moving permit lasts 30 days and requires back taxes to be paid first. When ownership changes, a name change permit is needed, and fines of up to $200 may apply. Call the Assessor at (843) 832-0162.

Farmland comes with a catch. Changing its use triggers a rollback of up to three years of tax savings, and the bill can land on whoever changes the use, which may be the new owner. The Assessor's site has a request form for a rollback estimate.

Send the assessor a written objection no later than 90 days after the notice goes in the mail. That is the rule in Section 12-60-2510 of the state code, and it reaches disputes about fair market value, special use value, the assessment ratio and the assessment as a whole.

A notice is required whenever fair market value climbs $1,000 or more and when a property is first assessed, usually by July 1. During a countywide reassessment, notices are due by October 1. With no notice at all, a written appeal is still possible at any time. Filed before the first penalty date, it covers that year; filed on or after, it covers the next. The Assessor can supply the current form.

sections.h2: Collection costs when taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
Fees climb through the year. In the most recent cycle the county added $35 to real property bills and $45 to mobile home bills in spring, a $35 posting fee in early summer and an $80 advertising charge by late October. Cards carry a 2.95 percent convenience fee and cannot be used to redeem property sold at a tax sale.

Cutoff dates for personal checks and for the last day to pay change each year, so ask the Delinquent Tax Office for the current schedule.

A few calls early save trouble later. Ask the Assessor whether your legal residence application is on file and whether any mobile home permits are open. Ask the Treasurer which office will send the next bill. Then request a payoff from the Delinquent Tax Office if anything is past due, since its fees change by date.

Keep a short list of what you learn: who you spoke to, the date and the figure they gave. Your closing agent will want the same details, and buyers sometimes ask whether the property's classification will change after the sale. The honest answer, for most sales in Dorchester County, is that it will be reappraised at market value as of December 31 of the sale year.

sections.h2: Selling a Dorchester County house with unpaid tax
sections.html:
A tax balance does not prevent a sale, though the tax, penalties and any collection fees all have to be paid off. Because fees change by date, a current payoff from the Delinquent Tax Office is the number to work from.

  1. Get the payoff and note the date through which it is good.
  2. Ask your closing agent how the payoff will be sent.
  3. Confirm the bill is addressed to the right owner.
  4. With a mobile home, ask the Assessor about permits and back taxes.

A cash sale avoids repair negotiations and a buyer's loan schedule, which helps when fees keep rising. We buy houses as they are, so send the address and the latest tax notice if you want an offer.

faqs.q: Is Dorchester County property tax due on January 15?
faqs.a: Yes. January 15 is the deadline, and a 3 percent penalty starts the following day. Another 7 percent comes after February 1 and 5 percent after March 16, reaching 15 percent.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the 4 percent legal residence rate in Dorchester County?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office, at (843) 832-0162. You can apply online or on paper, and paper forms are delivered to 201 Johnston Street in St. George.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Dorchester County if the property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, once the tax, penalties and collection fees are paid off. Get a payoff from the Delinquent Tax Office ahead of closing and settle with your closing agent how it will be sent.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Dorchester County assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days after the assessor mails the notice. Your objection must be written and addressed to the assessor.

faqs.q: Does the buyer's tax bill change after a sale?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A reappraisal at market value as of December 31 of the sale year is the usual result, so the new owner may pay a different amount.
